title: feat(apply): the apply flow runs the staged 4-step pipeline on both surfaces
body:
The apply flow now runs the staged quality pipeline instead of the one-shot fast path, and shows it as four visible steps — **Analyze → Generate → Validate → Remove AI signs** — identically from the Jobs page and from an Autopilot found-job apply. Third of five PRs in the multi-stage pipeline programme (after #990 projects normalization and #991 cover-letter + humanize stages).

## Why the apply flow couldn't run staged before

The run request could only resolve a job ad server-side out of the Jobs-page postings cache, so anything pasted or autopilot-sourced had no `jobId` and fell back to the one-shot path. The staged pipeline was reachable only from a jobs-only side panel.

## What changed

**IPC — a run can now start from text (`packages/shared`, `commands/resume_pipeline/`)**
`resumeId`/`jobId` default to empty; `resumeText`, `jobAdText`, `jobTitle`, `companyName`, `board` are accepted alongside them, with zod refinements requiring one of each pair. Resolution is an **id-wins rule**: a non-empty id means a store lookup and a hard error if it's missing — never a silent fallback to the text. `resolve_resume`/`resolve_job` are pure functions taking an id plus an injected lookup closure, so the text isn't even in scope on that path and a miss can only error. `sourceResumeId` is written only on the id path, which is what keeps #990's projects normalization from running against text of unknown provenance. Job-ad text reaches prompts exclusively through the existing `fenced("job_posting", …)` slot, so it inherits ADR-010 injection protection with no new primitive. `jobAdText` is now persisted into the record's `job_ad` (previously left deliberately empty on the text path).

**Retention** — a URL-less pasted job gets its own history slot via a hashed `unlinked_run_key` used only for `RunRow.job_url`, instead of every pasted job sharing one bucket.

**Résumé provenance (`ResumeInputCard`)** — the card surfaces which saved doc backs the current text, so the flow sends `resumeId` when the text is doc-backed and untouched, and `resumeText` once it's hand-edited. Pasted text is never silently imported. The card is seeded from a host-owned `docId` because it remounts on every wizard-step revisit; without the seed a post-remount edit compared against a local `null` and the host kept sending a stale doc id for text the user had since changed.

**TailorFlow runs the staged pipeline** — new `useTailorPipeline` wrapping `useResumePipelineSession`, reconnecting through a persisted run key. Stage events fold into four steps via a pure mapper (`analyze_job|match_evidence|strategy → Analyze`, `draft|cover_letter → Generate`, `validate|repair → Validate`, `humanize → Remove AI signs`; an unknown stage keeps the last). Numbered rows become checkmarks as stages finish, each with a one-line description, the thinking bubble, and the streaming pane. The depth picker is gone from the wizard. The fast-path tailor engine and its store are deleted, dead after the cutover.

## Review findings resolved in-branch

Four Opus reviews ran (rust-backend-architect, tauri-security-reviewer, frontend-reviewer, ui-ux-expert). Two rounds of blocking findings, all fixed and mutation-verified — each guard was reverted, watched go red, and restored:

- **Infinite update loop** — the run-persist effect had an unstable callback in its deps and no already-persisted guard, so persist → store update → new callback identity → refire. Fixed with a keyed guard plus a ref-held callback. The keying is itself asserted, so a legitimate second run still persists.
- **Cross-application run leak** — the persisted run key wasn't tied to an application, so opening application B could reconnect to A's run. Replaced with a self-describing `applyRun: { forId, runId, jobId }` read only when `forId` matches, correct on first render rather than via a reset effect. The reviewer confirmed the router does not remount on a param change, so the pre-existing `key={id}` on the page is a load-bearing part of this — noted for future readers.
- **A raw i18n key in the timed-out banner** — `pipeline.status.*` is `running/completed/needsReview/failed/cancelled` but the panel's own states are `done/needsReview/cancelled/error`, so a timed-out-but-saved run rendered the literal dotted key next to its stop reason, in both locales. The existing test could not catch it: a key-echoing `t` mock is structurally blind to a missing key. Fixed with an exhaustive `Record<TailorRunState, …>` (a new state fails to type-check until mapped) plus a test that asserts every reachable dynamic key against the **real** locale JSON.
- **Focus escaping an open dialog** — the stage-change focus effect fired against an open modal (the focus trap only intercepts Tab, not a programmatic `.focus()`), reachable via "start a run → open Interview questions → run finishes". Now bails when focus is inside `[aria-modal="true"]`, and no longer fires on mount.
- **Contrast** — the "all steps completed" confirmation and the streaming-target header were `text-foreground/45` (4.07:1 dark, below AA and below the `<14px` floor documented in `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`). Both at `/70` now. Every changed colour was independently recomputed in both themes, accounting for the light-scheme opacity lifts.
- Also: the 4th step now actually marks as done (including on the zero-cost humanize path), the panel fits the 900×600 floor with the thinking bubble collapsed by default, an elapsed timer keeps a long stage from looking frozen, a timed-out-but-saved run no longer reads as a clean success, a needsReview run with zero claims has a way forward, screen-reader users get per-row state plus a polite announcer that now also announces completion, and cancelling with no output is acknowledged.

Two items were deliberately left out of scope and are **not** regressions from this PR: the thinking-transcript contrast (3.75:1 light, pre-existing — worth its own ticket) and the elapsed-clock resetting on reconnect. One reviewer claim was refuted rather than acted on: the Cancel button was recomputed at 4.63:1 and passes AA as shipped.

## Testing

`pnpm typecheck` (13/13) · `pnpm test` (488 files / 7118 tests) · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · en/de key parity, zero orphans either direction · full Rust suite green via the pre-push hook.

Known gap, stated rather than papered over: the newly wired completion announcement can't fire in production today, because the panel unmounts before the step counter passes the last step. The durable completion signal is the results panel's own screen-reader line. The branch is wired correctly for when that changes and is covered directly by test.

body:
Pins the Rust toolchain so local builds, PR CI, and release builds stop being free to disagree.

## The problem

There was no `rust-toolchain.toml` and no `rust-version` in the crate manifest, and CI selected `stable` by ref name — `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@<sha> # stable`. So each surface got whatever `stable` meant that day.

Not hypothetical: a bare `cargo fmt --all` currently mass-reformats the repo, because some committed files predate the installed rustfmt, while the canonical files *do* pass `cargo fmt --check`. That is the signature of an unpinned formatter.

## The part that would have made a config-only fix useless

`dtolnay/rust-toolchain` **does not read `rust-toolchain.toml`.** Verified against the action's own source: the version comes entirely from which `@rev` you check out — `@stable` delegates to `rustup toolchain install stable` at runtime. Adding the config file alone would have pinned this machine while CI kept floating, and looked complete.

So every Rust job had to move onto a version-specific action revision. All 12 workflows were enumerated: 9 jobs go through `.github/actions/setup-rust`, and `release.yml` has its own inline setup step that does not use the composite action and needed the same change separately. The other 8 workflows touch no Rust at all.

## What it pins to, and why 1.97.1

`1.97.1` — what CI has actually been validating against (`stable` resolves there today; released 2026-07-16). An earlier revision of this branch pinned `1.96.1`, the version already installed locally, which read as a freeze from the dev machine but was silently a **downgrade for CI**. Pinning to what CI already ran preserves the tested configuration instead of reverting it; `rustup` fetches it locally from the toolchain file.

`rust-version = "1.95"` (MSRV) was derived from the dependency graph rather than picked: scanned `rust_version` across all resolved packages (744 of 1075 declare one). Highest floor is `sysinfo` at `1.95`; next is `serial_test` at `1.93.1`, a dev-dependency that `cargo test`/`clippy --all-targets` still compile. Cannot shift resolution — edition 2021 means resolver v2, and every CI invocation passes `--locked`.

## Deliberately not included

No `components` list in the toolchain file. Verified empirically that `rustup` *does* honour one — but also that the default profile already installs `rustfmt` and `clippy`, and the one specialist component (`llvm-tools-preview`, for coverage) is needed by a single job that already requests it. Listing them centrally just made every Rust job fetch things it does not use.

No `msrv` field in `clippy.toml`. It would surface `clippy::incompatible_msrv` findings unrelated to this change, and this PR is a pin, not an upgrade — flagged rather than silently skipped.

`release.yml`'s inline setup was left inline rather than refactored onto the shared composite action; it customises the cache key per macOS arch, which the composite action does not expose. Smallest diff wins.

## Testing

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean — no reformat was triggered, so there is nothing to land separately. `cargo test --workspace --locked` 4175 passed, identical to the run under the previous toolchain. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` clean. `pnpm gen:workflows:check` no drift. `pnpm typecheck` 13/13. `rustup show` confirms the pin resolves via the toolchain file.

Split out from the agentic-deletion PR deliberately: this is the one change that alters how everything compiles, so keeping it alone means a red run on either PR points somewhere unambiguous.

title: feat(pipeline): delete the max generation depth and the depth concept
body:
Deletes the `max` generation depth and the depth concept entirely. **86 files, +788 / −9051.** Fourth of five PRs in the multi-stage pipeline programme, after #990, #991 and #992.

## Why

`max` cost roughly 12+ model calls per run — a section-by-section fan-out plus an `llm_judge` stage whose output was Warning-only model opinion that nothing in the app acted on. That is pure token spend. #992 already cut the apply flow over to the staged quality pipeline unconditionally, so the depth selectors were steering a choice that no longer existed.

The staged pipeline is now the only one: `analyze_job → match_evidence → strategy → draft → cover_letter → validate → repair → humanize`.

## Deleted

**Rust** — `stages/judge.rs`, `stages/section_gen.rs`, `section_prompts.rs`, `max_pipeline()`/`MAX_STAGES`, `regenerate_max_entry`, the section-observer half of the run hooks, `Budget::RESUME_MAX`, `MAX_RUN_FIXED_SECS`, `GenerationDepth` and the request's `depth` field. `types_max.rs` trims to `ProjectOut` and `assemble.rs` to `render_project` — both load-bearing for #990's deterministic projects normalization.

**Renderer** — `DepthSelector`, `SectionTimeline`, `GenerationDepthPreferences`, the `useGenerationDepth` slice, `lib/generate/generation-depth.ts`, and the pipeline machine's per-section fold.

`TailoredResumePanel` survives this PR deliberately — see below.

## Existing user data keeps working

This is where a deletion this size actually fails, so it got the most attention. Three things are deliberately kept as read-only historic vocabulary, because users have runs recorded at all three depths:

- `RunRow.depth` stays a plain column, now always writing `"quality"`. **No migration** — verified correct by executing SQL probes that insert pre-deletion rows on retired stages and exercising the read, snapshot, write and import paths.
- `GENERATION_DEPTHS` in `packages/shared`, so an old `max` row renders "Max" rather than a raw token.
- `pipeline.stage.sections|assemble|llm_judge` translations.

That last one was a **caught regression, not a plan**. The first pass froze the depth vocabulary with a test, then deleted the stage names — which live on the *same rows*, of the *same feature*, rendered by the *same component* one line away. Review caught it by rendering a stored run and seeing three untranslated wire tokens next to a translated one. The fix-round enumeration then found two further render sites, because the live stage label replays from the last persisted event on reconnect.

## Behavior change worth stating

On a **historic `max` run**, regenerating one role (`SectionKey::Experience(n)`) no longer has its per-entry path, so it falls through to `regenerate_one_section` and rewrites the **whole Work Experience section**. The deleted path had guaranteed the opposite. This is inherent to deleting `max` and was already the documented degrade — no code change — but it is user-visible and belongs in the release notes.

## Review

`rust-backend-architect` APPROVE, `frontend-reviewer` BLOCK→resolved. Both ran every gate themselves and mutation-tested each claimed guard rather than reading them. Three findings are worth recording:

**Two functions went dead with zero signal.** An author verified a helper's last consumer and stopped one hop short — that consumer was itself deleted by this PR. Both are `pub` in a `pub` module of a lib crate, so `dead_code` structurally cannot fire; they survived 4175 tests, `clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, and the architecture suite. Found by deleting them and compiling. Applying the same method one hop further found a **third** (`sections::entry_range`, whose only callers lived in a test file this PR deletes) plus a chain of private helpers.

**A "guard" that only tested itself.** `PIPELINE_RUN_DEPTHS_HISTORIC` had zero production consumers — the component interpolates the label key directly. Truncating the constant reddened only the test's own assertion about the constant. Dropped; the label assertions that do hold were kept.

**The showcase separator lost its only pin.** Changing `PROJECT_SEPARATOR` from `" · "` to `" - "` passed the whole suite, because the deleted `max_test.rs` had held the only verbatim render assertions. That glyph feeds `consistency::tier_of` / `project_entry_starts` on the Projects section, so it is now pinned and mutation-tested.

## Scope note

`TailoredResumePanel` moves to PR-5. The first pass deleted it, then found it also hosts the agentic "Improve this résumé" flow, which nothing in the apply flow ports — so it reverted rather than orphaning a feature shipped six commits earlier. PR-5 already owns `improve_resume`, so the panel dies there alongside it. Here it keeps only the quality run: its depth picker and section timeline are gone, so nothing dead is left behind for a PR.

Also swept: the orphaned `pipeline.section.*` subtree (~17 keys × 2 locales), each verified unreferenced first — given the HIGH above is exactly what happens when a key looks dead and is not.

## Testing

`cargo test --workspace` 4175 passed / 26 ignored + 18 architecture + 3 eval · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` clean · `cargo fmt --check` · `gen:ipc:check` + `gen:prompts:check` · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm test` 485 files / 7118 tests · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · en/de parity, zero orphans.

body:
Owner-approved combined batch: six polish items plus the autopilot posting-date feature, one reviewable diff (42 files). Every item ran its own author → domain-critic → delta-verify chain; ~20 findings closed red-first along the way.

## Letters (export)

- **All six letter layouts stop hyphenating.** The four older layouts (Classic/Refined/Banded/Navy) justified without `hyphenate: false`, emitting U+00AD soft hyphens straight into the extracted text layer — the defect class #988 fixed for Sidebar/Monogram. The roster guard now covers the whole family, and a new test routes *every* layout through the choke point (extending the roster alone was a proven no-op — nothing exercised the old layouts). Justify stays on for all markets (full-measure columns; rivers are a non-issue). One preview SVG reflowed.
- **Nameless letters stop printing a date or salutation as the letterhead name.** `is_letterhead_name` (salutation/sign-off/subject/date) is ONE shared rule across PDF and both DOCX arms. Review caught the first version nesting the contact line under the new gate — a nameless letter with an attached contact profile lost both the date *and* the user's contact info in DOCX; contact now renders independently, mirroring the PDF, with `contact: Some(..)` as a mandated fixture axis (two prior tests hardcoding `None` is exactly how it shipped unverified). Bonus: salutation-opening letters had *never* emitted contact in DOCX — now they do. Suppression also exposed and fixed two latent Sidebar defects (a Typst `none.split` panic and an empty tinted rail).

## Small fixes

- **Company-brief cache key** now derives from `StageIdentity` wholesale (the canonical Completer→key-terms type, cross-referenced both ways) plus a new `Completer::search_backend()` term — review proved the resolved Native↔Exa backend flips on *credential presence at call time* and served the other vendor's brief for 7 days. Role is deliberately not a term (one paid search per company; documented as the cost tradeoff, not an omission).
- **Light-theme contrast, fixed centrally**: `text-foreground/15,/55,/60` + the entirely-uncovered `border-foreground/10–/25` family (73 call sites at `/10` alone, ~1.2:1 raw) join the remap. Folding `/60` in was forced by review math: mapped `/55` had overshot raw `/60`, inverting the token ordering — and raw `/60` was itself sub-AA despite a comment claiming otherwise. An ordering guard now pins `mapped(/55) < mapped(/60)`.
- **The dashboard AI-status widget stops lying in both directions.** Root cause: `system_health` probes only local Ollama, whatever provider is active — so cloud/CLI users saw a false "not available". The widget now uses the shared `useCanUseAI()` gate — whose `local-server` branch review then caught *never checking daemon liveness* (documented as "detected via a health probe"; no probe happened). The gate now requires `health.ai.ready` for Ollama with a distinct "Start Ollama" reason, healing all 14 call sites, and ships the repo's first unmocked test of the hook (every existing consumer test mocks it).
- **Italian AI-tell support**: a genuinely curated lexicon (13 lexical + 4 prose entries) through the four-rule checkability bar, frozen into the validators via the single-source `gen:prompts` path — Italian output already routed to the validators and simply fell into the uncurated empty arm. Review attacked every entry with truthful Italian sentences: `spirito di squadra` (a coach's real deliverable in object position) and `all'avanguardia` (the Futurist art movement) were demoted to prompt-only, each with a negative-control fixture in the entry's own surface form, mutation-checked by re-adding the entry. Elision makes apostrophe folding load-bearing in Italian (`l'esperienza`); proven by dual-spelling fixtures.

## Autopilot posting dates + per-card sorting

- **The posting date was parsed by every job board and dropped at one line** — `build_found_job` never copied it. It now threads through `FoundJob` (serde-defaulted; legacy stores load unchanged) with review-forced pins at both collapse points: `merge_found_jobs` (a mutation replacing the preserve-guard with an unconditional overwrite passed all 4115 tests until the new test) and `dedup_cross_source` (an Adzuna hit's date survived deduping against a dateless direct-board hit — previously lost permanently).
- **Each autopilot card sorts its own found-jobs list** (relevance default / newest / oldest), independently per card — the acceptance test renders two cards sorted differently at once. Sorting is a renderer-side view over a copy: the persisted order feeds AI-note recipient selection (ADR-020) and a dedicated non-mutation test pins that. Dated rows band before undated ones in *both* directions (a `?? 0` fallback regression is invisible in the descending sort — both are tested). Date chips reuse the Jobs page's relative-time helper; en+de keys.

## Also in this diff

`docs/NEXT_ISSUES.md` (the old deferred-items ledger, in-repo since July) is retired per owner decision — deleted, gitignored, every citation across docs/CSS/Rust comments reworded to stand alone.

4137 Rust lib + architecture suite, full JS suite, clippy `--all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings`, fmt, `gen:ipc:check` + `gen:prompts:check`, eslint root + a11y — all green on the combined tree. Zero new dependencies.

title: fix: generation-burst reliability and the silent defects from the 2026-08-08 diagnostics bundle
body:
Everything here comes from one support bundle (`ajh-diagnostics-2026-08-08`, app 0.134.3): six applications imported, six résumé + cover-letter generations fired within 62 seconds on `ollama-cloud` / `gpt-oss:20b`.

## What the log actually showed

| run | started  | outcome                                    |
| --- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | 19:56:14 | done — 8m37s                               |
| 2   | 19:56:32 | **failed — HTTP 429 after 8m55s**          |
| 3   | 19:56:43 | done — 11m28s                              |
| 4   | 19:56:51 | done — 13m14s                              |
| 5   | 19:57:09 | done — 12m44s                              |
| 6   | 19:57:16 | done — 11m40s                              |

**Peak 7 concurrent AI streams** against a documented cap of 3. The same workload on `gemma4:31b` earlier that day took 12–23 _seconds_ per run; `gpt-oss:20b` emitted 1,039,821 chars of reasoning against 45,416 of answer (22.9:1).

Worse than the one visible failure: **all six cover letters were written for a nonsense company** (`You'll Do` ×3, `experience **fast`, `the core of their product. You'll sit at the intersection of design`, `a **bootstrapped AI platform and consulting studio** based in Munich`) and **all six had zero company research**. None of it surfaced — the 27,601-line log contained exactly one `ERROR`, and 27,178 lines were a single repeated Tauri warning.

## Commits

| commit     | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ac8e0205` | Company name: the fallback regex alternated on a bare `at` with no word boundary, matching inside "Wh**at** You'll Do". `sanitizeCompanyName` now gates both the model's JSON and the regex; the bare `catch {}` that hid which ran is a warn.                       |
| `5074e14e` | **The concurrency cap was enforced on `ai_generate`, which the tailoring flow doesn't call.** `generate_pipeline` acquired nothing — no rate window, no slot, no daily charge. Now takes a slot via a new `acquire_queued` that waits rather than rejects, on the same semaphore. The renderer re-arms its deadline while queued. |
| `fc5863a0` | Research was bounded by a flat 25s around search **and** synthesis — a cap on how much reasoning the model was allowed. Now scales by effort off the same table `stream_deadline` uses. `salary_research` had the identical copy.                                    |
| `ece8d890` | Failed spans logged at INFO; `[ai] →`/`←` had nothing to pair them; 98.5% of the bundle was Tauri's stale-callback warning (one per streamed delta).                                                                                                                |
| `f34bf4c9` | Every HTTP 400 was `qwen3-embedding:8b` on `/api/chat`. `reachable_chat_model` returned `/api/tags`'s first entry — it was a health probe reused as "give me a chat model".                                                                                          |
| `80ace1b5` | A stream's initial 429 was never retried, on the reasoning that "a mid-stream restart duplicates deltas" — but the status arrives before any delta.                                                                                                                 |
| `75e07dc7` | Role extraction searched for `Jetzt bewerben` and `[← Alle offenen Stellen](/karriere)`. Also fixes the Rust twin of the `at` bug.                                                                                                                                  |
| `dd727531` | 1,932 rejected handshakes × 2 log lines each; `crashes.log` entries truncated mid-backtrace.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `b41de019` | A reasoning-heavy run now says so instead of looking hung.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Verified

`cargo test --all-features` (3265) · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` clean · all 18 architecture rules · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · `pnpm test` (5014).

Every guard added here is mutation-tested — neutering `QueueSlot::drop`, leaking a permit, dropping the timeout re-arm, removing the chat-model filter, removing the log suppression, and removing the ratio check each fail a test.

## Not fixed, deliberately

- The `cannot move state from Destroyed` panic is third-party teardown I could not reproduce; a speculative guard would be worse than the next real backtrace, which is now capturable.
- The extension's ~10s reconnect is correct behaviour — browsers don't expose a failed WS handshake's HTTP status, so it genuinely cannot tell "refused" from "not running". Only the logging changed.

## Review notes

- `commands/ai.rs` and `ai_provider/mod.rs` were both at the R8 LOC cap, so this extracts `admit_research` (the ~40-line preamble three research commands repeated verbatim) and moves `RequestTrace` to its own module. Both are pure extractions.
- The architecture test caught an L2→L3 import in my first attempt at the research deadline; it's now injected by the L3 caller, matching how `SalaryResearch::enrich` already takes its cache.
- Pushed with `--no-verify` at the author's request, so the pre-push AI review gate did not run; the checks listed above were run manually.

title: feat: add exa as a fallback web-search backend for company research
body:
Company research ran on **the active AI provider's own web search**, which left a whole population with nothing:

- **`openai-compatible` gateways** report `supports_web_search: false` — every LM Studio / vLLM / OpenRouter / Groq / Together / DeepSeek user got no research at all.
- **Local Ollama** reports `supports_web_search: true` for the _family_, but the Ollama Web Search API needs a separate **ollama.com account key**. A keyless install showed the "search company" toggle **ON** and returned an empty brief every single time.

The second is worse, because nothing surfaced it. The 2026-08-08 bundle that drove #960 showed the cost: six cover letters written with no company knowledge, indistinguishable from six written with a full brief — plus 28 lifetime `no usable brief (provider found nothing)` lines no user would ever see.

## The seam already existed

`research.rs` was already provider-agnostic (the `SearchResult` shape, query builders, synthesis prompts, injection guard), and the three `ollama_research*` functions were each:

```
search → if empty return "" → synthesize with the provider's own model
```

**Only the search step was ever Ollama-specific.** So this is a search-backend swap, not a new research pipeline.

## What changed

| commit     | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `efd0c974` | `WebSearcher` trait + `ExaSearcher` (`api.exa.ai/search`, `ai:exa`). The three pipelines move to `search/` as `searched_research*`, so company / salary / per-question answers all gain the fallback at once.               |
| `1414c4a0` | `supportsWebSearch` reports whether research can actually **run**, not what the provider advertises. Plus the Exa key slot in Settings → Company Research.                                                                   |
| `d50f536e` | ADR-0023, the **search backend** glossary term, README/SECURITY egress enumeration, and two already-stale fixes in `anti-abuse-limits.md`.                                                                                  |

## Three decisions, each with a real alternative

1. **Fallback only, resolved from configuration before any call.** A provider that can already search keeps its own search *even with an Exa key stored* — nobody silently starts paying a second vendor. `resolve_search_backend` is a pure predicate so the rule is pinned by a test, not convention; inverting it fails that test.
2. **No second chance.** A native search that runs and returns empty is not retried against Exa. It would rescue the 28 observed empty briefs, but costs a second billable call on every miss and lets two vendors see one query.
3. **Synthesis stays on the user's own model.** Exa's `/answer` would be fewer calls but bypasses both `SYNTH_SYSTEM`'s prompt-injection guard (search results are attacker-reachable text, and this is the one stage that reads them unfenced) and the `is_no_info` filter.

The fallback lands on the `AiProvider::research` **default**, so providers with native search override it and are untouched, and a new provider with no search inherits it — no per-provider change either way.

## Behaviour change worth a release note

A keyless Ollama user who sees the research toggle **ON** today will see it **OFF** after this. That is the bug being fixed — the toggle was promising a brief it could never produce — but it is visible.

## Egress

No ADR-0005 amendment. Exa is a new _vendor_ inside the already-enumerated **class 3 (web search, opt-in)**, not a new egress class, and it is opt-in by construction — nothing is sent until a key is stored. It receives exactly what the current search already does (company name, role title, question topic); never résumés, generations, applications or credentials. Rust-side via `net::http`, so no CSP change. Exa charges its own `(day, vendor)` daily bucket rather than spending the AI provider's.

## Verified

`cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` clean · `cargo test --all-features` (3277, incl. all 18 architecture rules) · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · `pnpm format:check` · `pnpm test` (5028).

Mutation-checked: making `resolve_search_backend` prefer Exa fails the fallback-only test.

## Review notes

- `ai_provider/mod.rs` sits at the R8 LOC cap, so the new code is its own module; the two new trait methods carry deliberately tight docs to stay under it.
- One thing this PR does **not** do: surface Exa's `costDollars` (returned per response) into the spend store. The store is token-shaped and a real per-search cost deserves its own change.

## Why

Search Console (Aug 8, 2026) flagged `aijobhunter.app`: 4 indexed / 18 not indexed. Most of the 18 are benign — http→https and www→apex redirects, `?ref=` variants covered by canonical, and Cloudflare's `/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection` 404. The real signal is five pages Google will not serve:

| URL | State |
| --- | --- |
| `/accessibility`, `/agent-system`, `/architecture-map`, `/how-it-works` | Discovered – currently not indexed, **last crawled `N/A`** |
| `/world` | Crawled, not indexed (WebGL page, near-zero text — expected) |
| `/tech-radar` | Not in any Search Console bucket yet |

Nothing was blocking them: all return 200, none carry `noindex`, `robots.txt` is `Allow: /`, and the sitemap reads Success (10 URLs, last read Aug 8).

## What

**1. Home footer had drifted from the doc-page footer.** `SiteFooter` links `/agent-system`, `/architecture-map`, `/tech-radar` and `/storybook/`; the home `Finale` foot-nav did not. Those routes were reachable only from pages Google has not fetched yet, so they sat one hop behind an uncrawled page — and `/` is the only URL on this domain with real crawl equity. Same orphan class #934 fixed for `/how-it-works`.

**2. `HomeBody.test.tsx` asserts the invariant**: every sitemap route (except `/`) is linked from home. Mutation-checked — removing any one link fails it.

**3. Sitemap entries carry `lastmod`**, hand-kept from each route's last content-bearing commit rather than a build timestamp. A fresh date on every deploy is exactly the churn Google learns to distrust; too-old is the safe failure direction.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @ajh/landing test` — 338 passed (37 files)
- `pnpm lint:strict` clean · `tsc --noEmit` clean
- Built `out/sitemap.xml` carries `<lastmod>`; built `out/index.html` links all 10 routes
- Pre-push gate: parity OK, agent-system in sync, AI review clean

Indexing is still gated on crawl budget for a young domain — the remaining lever is **Request indexing** per URL in Search Console, which is a manual step on the account.

title: feat: deterministic content validation and quality report for generated documents
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the multi-stage resume pipeline programme: every generated résumé and cover letter is now **deterministically validated against the candidate's own source document**, with the result persisted, surfaced in the UI, and available to the agent. The core rule made mechanical: the LLM decides HOW to present verified evidence — these validators catch it deciding WHAT.

- **`validate/content/`** (L1): 25-code deterministic validator family — factual (unsourced metrics/terms/dates, dropped roles, altered project links), alignment (coverage regression vs source, missing evidenced requirements), consistency (dates, title drift, skills claimed-but-not-demonstrated, project-structure tiers), duplicates, ATS structure + keyword-density, and a `voice.*` anti-AI-tell family (single-source lexicon shared with the generation prompts via codegen). Criticals come only from deterministic checks — a model can never emit one.
- **`documents/evidence.rs`** (L1): evidence extraction (`extract_evidence`/`rank_bullets`) — the `rank_trim_candidates` core moved out of the R8-frozen `match_resume.rs` (net −141 lines, trim-panel wire-compat pinned by test).
- **`quality_report` on `ai_generations`** (ADR-007 §F2): opaque wrapper JSON, per-top-level-key merge, full backup/restore round-trip, 256 KB clamps on both write paths.
- **`resume:validateContent` IPC** (5-step): server-side clamps, strict docKind, content-free spans (ADR-027).
- **Four agent Read tools**: `validate_resume`, `search_candidate_evidence`, `lookup_salary`, `get_trim_suggestions` — fenced, clamped, least-privilege-pinned; fence-tag registry + `tool_result` marker hardened against forgery (incl. nested-marker bypass).
- **`pnpm gen:prompts` codegen**: the anti-AI-tell lexicon is generated from `natural-voice.ts` into Rust with a CI drift gate — one source instructs the model and validates its output, guarded in both directions.
- **Renderer**: integrity badge + QualityReportPanel (evidence-first, guidance-framed, en+de), report-carrying saves, staleness via source-text hash, Re-check action, hand-edit nudge.

## Review trail

Five domain critics + a security review + a 3-pass `/review` ensemble with per-finding fresh-context verification ran before this PR. Every blocking finding was fixed with mutation-verified regression tests, including: six false-positive Criticals on truthful documents, a per-key merge defect, a forged-fence-tag hole, a renderer cancel race, a UTF-8 boundary panic on accented URLs (`café-berlin.de`) that would have aborted the app mid-generation, and a malformed-persisted-report renderer crash. Zero verifier-rejected findings; ledger updated.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --lib`: 3410 passed · `--test architecture`: 18/18 · clippy `-D warnings` clean
- Desktop vitest: 3074 passed · prompts 742 · workspace typecheck 13/13 · `lint:strict` clean
- `gen:ipc:check` + `gen:prompts:check` clean · backup/export round-trip covers the new column
- Fixtures include paraphrased-but-truthful en+de documents (zero-Critical guards) and accented-URL project entries

body:
## Summary

Phase 2 (structured-output half) of the multi-stage résumé pipeline programme: `complete_structured(app, req, schema_hint)` on the `AiProvider` trait with a prompt-discipline default, native overrides where the wire format is verified, and a pure, hardened JSON extraction/repair/parse module for the pipeline stages that will consume it. This is deliberate forward surface — zero production callers yet; `Completer::complete_json` (which must charge `record_usage` itself) wires it up in the next phase.

- **openai** — `response_format: json_schema` (strict mode) via new `openai_body.rs`; schema `strictify` with depth cap and whole-degrade to `json_object` on composition keywords it can't walk
- **gemini** — `responseSchema` translation via new `gemini_body.rs`; kept-keyword set verified against the current Schema reference (incl. `pattern`, `minimum`/`maximum`, length/property bounds); degrades to `responseMimeType` + hint when a schema can't be translated whole
- **ollama** — native `format` field; **ollama_cloud** delegates through the OpenAI-compatible layer (`response_format` support cited to vendor docs)
- **anthropic** — deliberately NO override: older models take the prompt-discipline default; no guessed beta wire format
- **`pipeline/json.rs`** — candidate-ordered `extract`/`repair`/`parse<T>`: whole-response first, fenced bodies last-first, balanced spans last-first, containment-aware repair ordering, content-free `Display`/`Debug` on the error type, ADR-010-fenced `reask_detail()`
- `req.effort` threads through all three native structured paths using the same per-provider gates as the streaming bodies
- `pagination.rs` split out of `ai_provider/mod.rs` (mechanical); dead `supportsStructuredOutput` flag removed from `packages/prompts` + renderer + docs

## Internal review (pre-PR gates)

- `tauri-security-reviewer` (BLOCK → fixed): fence-inside-string-value extraction hijack, `Debug` leaking withheld model content (Sentry-reachable), provenance-dropping prompt join, unfenced re-ask detail, case-sensitive role match, unbounded schema recursion — all reproduced red first, fixed, mutation-checked
- 3-pass `pr-reviewer` ensemble (opus + 2× sonnet) + verification: 7 further findings fixed (containment-aware repair ordering incl. executed PoCs, sibling anti-decoy pinning test, effort threading, strict-mode composition-keyword degrade on both translators, Gemini constraint keywords, empty-hint directive, `extract_json` trap removal)
- cleanup audit: zero dead code; one doc drift fixed (`ARCHITECTURE.md` provider-profile description)

## Gates

`cargo fmt` · `clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` · `cargo test --all-features --lib` (3626) · `--test architecture` (18) · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint:strict` · `@ajh/prompts` vitest (750) — all green.
